newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Clinton praises Barshefsky over WTO infotech pact.
newsitem.headline: Clinton praises Barshefsky over WTO infotech pact.

text.p: President Bill Clinton telephoned Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky on Friday to congratulate her on her efforts to win an agreement this week on information technology trade, U.S. officials said.
"The president was very pleased," said a U.S. spokesman.
Barshefsky, who has been acting U.S. trade representative since earlier this year when Mickey Kantor left to become commerce secretary, is expected to be officially named U.S. trade representative.
But the spokesman said the president did not discuss the job offer with Barshefsky during his 10-minute telephone conversation with her.

He said the two spoke only about the World Trde Organisation conference and the successful conclusion of an Information Technology Agreement that will eliminate tariffs on computers, software and other information products by 2000.
Administration officials in Washington said Clinton may announce some economic cabinet posts on Friday, but it was unclear whether Barshefsky's expected appointment would be announced at that time.
After the conclusion of the WTO ministerial meeting on Friday, Barshefsky was to head to Tokyo, where she faces tough negotiations to settle a bilateral dispute over Japan's insurance market.
She is due to return to Washington by Monday for a U.S.-European Union summit.
